To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the planning problem of reconciling two ontologies is undecidable, (2) it is not possible to automatically translate from a service description in one ontology to a service description in another ontology, and (3) it is possible to translate from one service description to another service description, provided that the ontologies are reconciled in advance, and that the translation is performed by a software agent that has the ability to rearrange the structure of the message it is sending.

(a) it is possible to automatically translate between ontologies that differ in the way they describe the same domain, and (b) it is possible for an agent to automatically rearrange its data structures to match the expectations of another agent.
A planning system that can handle ontological mismatches can also automatically restructure the internal data structures of messages so they match the recipient's expectations, and vice versa."

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed techniques to allow a service agent, when receiving a message from a client agent, to transform its data structures to match the client's expectations, even if the service agent's data structures are not directly compatible with those of the client.
it is possible to have agents with different ontologies interact, but only if the data structures of one agent are rearranged to match those of the other.
it is feasible to build a system that can take a description of a service, written in a formal language, and automatically generate an agent that can provide that service.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, even though the Semantic Web is a grand vision of a future that may never be realized, there is still much to learn from the effort to realize it.
, in order for agents to communicate with each other, they must have a common ontology, and they must agree on how to interpret the data structures in messages that they exchange.
the "Semantic Web", as envisioned in this way, will be more complex to implement than the Web of today.
